description.short_caption: Frontal chest and abdominal radiograph showing thoracic and abdominal structures.
description.detailed_description: This is a frontal radiograph of the chest and abdomen, likely from a pediatric patient based on skeletal proportions. The thoracic cavity shows clear lung fields without obvious consolidation, pleural effusion, or masses. The cardiac silhouette appears normal in size and shape. The abdominal cavity reveals gas-filled bowel loops, with no apparent signs of obstruction or abnormal calcifications. The bony structures, including ribs, spine, and pelvis, appear intact without visible fractures or deformities.

This image is a barium swallow radiograph demonstrating the esophagus. There is a clear narrowing of the esophageal lumen, likely due to a stricture or external compression. The contrast medium outlines the esophagus, highlighting the abnormality. The surrounding anatomy is faintly visible, consistent with the imaging technique.

description.short_caption: Barium swallow showing a dilated esophagus with a narrowed distal segment.
description.detailed_description: This is a barium swallow radiograph demonstrating a markedly dilated esophagus with a smooth, tapered narrowing at the distal end, resembling a 'bird-beak' appearance. The contrast medium outlines the esophageal lumen, highlighting the obstruction at the gastroesophageal junction. The surrounding anatomy is faintly visible, and no obvious perforation or extravasation of contrast is seen.
